runs.scope: Phase 3 candidate #5 — release-version drift checker. Turns the v0.3.0 inline-comment convention (every hardcoded version fallback documents its lockstep-with-pyproject.toml requirement) into an automated check that can run under CI or as a pre-release hook. Stdlib-only Python 3.11+ script with a declarative registry of all ten call sites. Docs-first: MS-DES-0005 landed before the implementation.
runs.notes: Docs-first: MS-DES-0005 drafted before the first line of script code. Rejected in the Alternatives section: (A) magic-marker comments scattered across five source files, (B) third-party tools (bump2version, bumpver, commitizen) — they want to own the bump, not just the check, and add dependencies with their own config languages, and (C) inline per-file assertions that would turn a release-time concern into a runtime failure and force pyproject.toml to be readable at import time in every deployment. Picked a Python-constant registry inside the script itself so 'what do I need to bump on release?' has exactly one answer (read CALL_SITES in check_release_versions.py). Implementation (~400 lines including heavy inline commentary): dataclass `CallSite(path, pattern, description)` with a compiled-regex contract (exactly one capture group; registry-level assertion raises SystemExit(2) if violated). Canonical source is `pyproject.toml [project].version` via stdlib `tomllib` (3.11+). Ten call sites covered: the three pyproject.toml version literals (canonical, Flet `app.build_version`, Briefcase `[tool.briefcase].version`), `version.py` `__version__`, `middleware/config/system_config.json` `version` field, and the five Python fallbacks in cli/main.py, bootstrap.py, middleware/storage/schemas.py, middleware/storage/models.py, gui/modules/auto_update_manager.py. Briefcase site uses a multi-line regex anchored to the `[tool.briefcase]` section header to distinguish it from the two same-file peers. Output: human-readable drift report by default, `--json` for CI. Exit codes: 0 in-sync, 1 drift, 2 usage error. Missing call-site files → exit 1 with `found: null` (drift, not error) per MS-DES-0005 §Error handling. Missing or malformed pyproject.toml → exit 2 with structured stderr message (no Python traceback). Tests: 12 unit tests in plain `unittest` (no pytest dependency), all passing in ~7ms. `_RepoFixture` helper builds an isolated tmp-dir fake repo with configurable version literal per site — no test touches the real repo. Coverage includes all three exit codes (0/1/2), JSON schema conformance, pyproject-peer-version drift (Briefcase stuck while canonical moves), missing-call-site drift, registry discipline (exactly-10-sites tripwire, one-capture-group invariant). End-to-end validation against the real v0.3.0 repo: `python3 build_scripts/check_release_versions.py` under the 3.12 venv reports 'All 10 site(s) in sync at version 0.3.0' — zero drift. Deliberate drift injection (schemas.py Pydantic default temporarily stomped to 0.2.0): report correctly flagged middleware/storage/schemas.py:110 with expected=0.3.0 / found=0.2.0 / context='version: str = "0.2.0"' and exit 1. MS-DES-0005 acceptance criteria #1, #2, #3, #4, #5, #6, and #7 all objectively verified. style-checker --check on the two new Markdown files (docs/design/release-checklist-script.md, CHANGELOG.md) clean on first pass — no manual fixes needed. No PROPER_NOUNS friction this time because the design spec avoided embedding bare 'SQLite' or 'OpenClaw' in headings (lesson learned from runs #7 and #9). Phase 3 candidate #5 complete.

runs.scope: Phase 3 candidate #3 — pipeline-log utility-scoring analyzer. Turns the 11-run docs/.doc-pipeline-log.json dataset into a read-only, stdlib-only analyzer that emits a per-skill scorecard in human, JSON, or Markdown form. Closes the 'nine structured runs is enough to start computing per-skill numbers' observation from the Phase 2 retrospective.
runs.notes: Docs-first: MS-DES-0006 drafted before the analyzer script. Alternatives considered and rejected in the design spec: (A) self-reporting `skills_invoked` field on each run — would require backfilling the eleven existing entries, is fragile to future omissions, and the inferred heuristic is tight enough that self-reporting would be redundant; (B) full bootstrap confidence intervals on every proportion — at n=11 most 95% CIs would span more than half the possible range, so reporting them would imply more rigor than the data supports; (C) third-party visualization (Jupyter / matplotlib / dashboards) — eleven rows fits on one terminal screen. Attribution model (six rules, one per underlying skill): doc-freshness attributed when docs_scanned > 0; style-checker when fixes or warnings are non-zero OR notes/scope mention style-checker artifacts OR a Rule-NN.N regex hits; changelog-writer when CHANGELOG.md appears in created_files or files_modified; release-notes when any docs/release-notes-*.md appears; doc-generator when any docs/api/ path appears OR notes mention doc-generator/extract_signatures.py; doc-pipeline unconditionally (every run IS a pipeline run). Rules live as top-level plain functions keyed by skill name in a single ATTRIBUTION_RULES dict so 'why did run #N count toward skill X?' is answerable by reading one function body. Implementation (~650 lines including heavy inline commentary): pure-function `analyze(runs)` returns (per_skill_metrics, overall_metrics); PerSkillMetrics + OverallMetrics dataclasses; three formatters dispatched through a FORMATTERS dict; argparse CLI with --log-path and --format. Stdlib-only (json, pathlib, argparse, statistics, re, dataclasses, datetime, collections.Counter, typing). Per-skill metrics: utilization rate, coverage file count, runs-invoked list. Skill-specific extras: style-checker (total_errors_fixed, mean, max, current_warnings_backlog last-observed); doc-freshness (totals + fresh_rate); changelog-writer (edits + stamp events); release-notes (created count); doc-generator (api_docs_touched); doc-pipeline (runs_logged). Overall metrics: total_runs, log_span_days, runs_per_week, longest_gap_days, docs_first_discipline_rate (MS-DES-NNNN references / total), release_cut_runs (tightened regex — see below), latest_release_date, days_since_latest_release. Tests: 48 unit tests in plain unittest (no pytest dependency), all passing in ~7ms. Four test classes map to MS-DES-0006 AC #7 (a) attribution per skill, (b) metric arithmetic on a three-run fixture, (c) all three output formatters, (d) empty-log edge case. Initial end-to-end run against the real 11-run log surfaced a false-positive: release_cut_runs reported [9, 11] because run #11's scope mentions 'release-version drift checker' which substring-matched 'release'. Tightened the heuristic to require either a version literal directly followed by the word 'release' (`v0.3.0 release`) or the exact phrase 'release cut'. MS-DES-0006 §Overall metrics updated to document the rationale. Added regression test `test_release_cut_rejects_incidental_release_mentions` to lock the rejection behavior against decoys like 'release-version drift checker', 'treating all history through v0.2.0 as the scan range', and 'capturing lessons from the v0.3.0 cut'. Baseline scorecard captured at docs/analysis/pipeline-log-baseline-2026-04-14.md: style-checker 73% utilization / 20 errors fixed / 22 backlog; changelog-writer 82% / 9 edits / 1 stamp event; doc-freshness 45% / 39 docs scanned / 0.949 fresh rate; doc-generator 27% / 2 API-ref touches; release-notes 27% / 2 drafted; doc-pipeline 100% / 11 runs. Interpretation notes in the baseline call out the bursty log window (77 runs/week artifact — all 11 runs fell across two calendar days), the midway docs-first adoption, and the note-only attribution of run #8 as caveats. style-checker --check on the three new Markdown files (MS-DES-0006 spec, baseline report, CHANGELOG) clean on first pass — no manual fixes. Phase 3 candidate #3 complete.

runs.scope: Phase 3 candidate #1 — Rule 3.1 sentence-case hardening. Closes the two failure modes the v0.3.0 cycle learned the hard way were real: (1) PROPER_NOUNS allowlist gap (OpenClaw was being lowercased to 'openclaw'), (2) sentence-boundary unawareness in multi-sentence headings (## One Repo. One Learning Agent. was collapsing to '## One repo. one learning agent.'). Both bugs jointly made it unsafe to batch-apply style_autofix.py against README.md, which held 22 Rule-3.1 findings — the baseline backlog at run #12. With the two bugs fixed, the entire backlog was addressable as a single clean sweep, retiring the 22-finding (actually 21 — one was a duplicate of a fix that had landed via a different path) backlog to zero.
runs.notes: Docs-first: MS-DES-0007 drafted before touching style_autofix.py. Three alternatives rejected in the design spec: (A) extract PROPER_NOUNS to a YAML / JSON config file — rejected because the ~60-entry dict is governance-surfaced cleanly via PR, config-file indirection adds a stdlib-limited YAML dep for no current payoff, and proper-noun spellings are a technical decision the style guide should own; (B) support multi-word proper nouns (react native, claude code) via a tokenizer-aware pass — rejected because none of the 22 README findings needed it, adding look-ahead turns the simple pass into a finite-state machine with backtracking semantics, and the backtick-wrapping escape hatch (`Claude Code`) already passes through verbatim; (C) plug in nltk.tokenize.PunktSentenceTokenizer or spaCy — rejected because the stdlib-first house convention has now shipped seven skills without a third-party NLP dep, headings are <10 tokens so period detection with a technical-identifier carve-out is a 10-line helper not a 50MB model, and any model error would be silent while a regex-and-punctuation-list rule is inspectable in one function body. Implementation: (1) PROPER_NOUNS widened from ~30 to ~60 entries, organized with category comments: added OpenClaw, SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, iOS, Flet, Briefcase, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, plus the acronym block API / CLI / SDK / UI / IDE / GUI / OSS / BSD / MIT / TLS / HTTP / HTTPS / URL / AST / NFKC / RRF. (2) Added _SENTENCE_TERMINATORS frozenset = {'.', '!', '?'} and _ends_sentence(core, trailing) helper that returns True only when trailing is exactly one terminator character (ellipsis '...' has trailing length 3, version literal 'v0.3.0' has a period internal to a technical identifier that _is_technical_identifier already catches — neither flips state). (3) Rewrote _sentence_case_heading to thread at_sentence_start state (replacing the first_word_seen flag): starts True, after each content token it re-evaluates via _ends_sentence(core, trailing). When True, next token gets 'first word' treatment (leading cap); when False, existing lowercase-or-passthrough logic applies. Tests: 12 new unit tests in test_style_autofix.py (45 total, all passing in ~80ms). Coverage: each added PROPER_NOUNS entry (OpenClaw, SQLite/PostgreSQL/MySQL, iOS, GitHub, Flet/Briefcase/Pydantic/SQLAlchemy), five sentence-boundary cases (period, question mark, exclamation mark, ellipsis non-terminator, version-literal non-terminator), registry invariants (no lowercase values, openclaw key present). Sweep: python3 skills/style-checker/scripts/style_autofix.py README.md produced 21 heading fixes in a single pass (one fewer than baseline — the pre-sweep README had been subtly touched between baseline capture and sweep). Post-sweep verification: python3 skills/style-checker/scripts/style_autofix.py --check README.md reports 'clean' — MS-DES-0007 AC #1 satisfied. Notable confirmed-correct transformations: '## Memento-Skills vs OpenClaw' unchanged (OpenClaw preserved via PROPER_NOUNS); '## One Repo. One Learning Agent.' → '## One repo. One learning agent.' (sentence-boundary state correctly flipping after the first period); '## What Is Memento-Skills?' → '## What is Memento-Skills?' (hyphenated proper noun preserved); '### GUI Enhancements' → '### GUI enhancements' (acronym preserved); '### IM Platform Integration (New)' → '### IM platform integration (new)' (parenthetical lowercased). Style-guide Rule 3.1 prose extended with (a) a multi-sentence-headings subsection with a Good/Bad pair and an ellipsis/version-literal non-terminator note, (b) a proper-nouns subsection pointing at PROPER_NOUNS as the authoritative source with instruction to extend in the same PR as new proper nouns. Style-check of the three new/modified Markdown files (MS-DES-0007 spec, CHANGELOG) clean; style-guide.md has 48 pre-existing findings (45 Rule-3.1 title-case headings that predate the autofixer + 3 demonstration strings inside Bad examples) which are out of MS-DES-0007 scope and documented as such. Successor baseline captured at docs/analysis/pipeline-log-baseline-2026-04-14-readme-swept.md (distinct filename so the pre-sweep baseline stays immutable). Phase 3 candidate #1 complete.
